technical_facts: Implemented early 3D navigation in games where characters moved in a 3D space, causing startle reactions in users unfamiliar with the perspective.
First program written was '10 print John Carmack' on a TRS80 computer.
Used 'go to' statements in early BASIC programming due to a lack of structured loops (for, while), though he avoids them in modern code except in low-level infrastructure.
Developed a scrolling hack on Apple II by leveraging the hardware's text-screen scrolling capability to scroll low-resolution graphics.
Used C++ (C-flavored) for serious programming and Python for AI/ML work, noting Python's inefficiency in loops compared to GPU tensor operations.
Advocated for the simplicity of C and Go, noting that simple languages are easier for engineers to jump into and maintain over long periods.
Views garbage collection as a net positive for most software to avoid memory safety vulnerabilities common in C/C++.
Implemented 'adaptive tile refresh' for early PC scrolling games, redrawing only changed tiles to increase frame rates.
Discovered that graphics memory on certain VGA cards wrapped around, allowing for smooth scrolling by drawing only one new line of tiles.
Developed 'compiled scalars' for Wolfenstein 3D, creating optimized assembly routines for specific image heights to accelerate scaling.
Used ray casting for Wolfenstein 3D, casting rays from the origin to find wall intersections in a tiled world.
Implemented Binary Space Partitioning (BSP) trees in Doom to provide a fixed ordering of surfaces for efficient rendering.
Developed Quake as a true 3D engine with 6 degrees of freedom, surface caching, and a client-server networking model over TCP/IP.
Created QuakeC, a pseudo-object-oriented language for modding the game's logic.
Advocated for OpenGL over Direct3D to maintain an open standard that eventually benefited mobile graphics (OpenGL ES).
Utilized static analysis tools to scrub large codebases, finding a high regularity of errors like incorrect printf format strings and missing null checks.
Prefers using asserts in private code (10-20% of the code) to catch logical errors and world-view shifts.
personality_patterns: Highly consistent work ethic, typically working 60 hours a week (10 hours a day, 6 days a week).
Avoids all-nighters, noting that cognitive productivity drops significantly after 12 hours.
Driven by 'user value' as the primary metric for success, rather than technical elegance or 'CodeGolf' puzzles.
Possesses an 'obsessive' personality trait, finding happiness in pushing through difficult technical problems.
Unsentimental about his early work, believing he could do a better job on every project he's ever completed.
Prefers a 'full-stack' understanding, from hardware registers up to high-level design.
Maintains a ritualistic approach to work, including consuming 8-9 Diet Cokes a day.
Values directness and efficiency, often pushing for 'speed of light' solutions.
Avoids 'fictional users' in design, insisting on analyzing data from real users.

gnosis_principles.description: All engineering efforts should flow from the value provided to the user; technical pride in architecture is secondary to the net value created for the person using the product.

heritage_patterns: The 'Hacker Ethic': Sharing information and source code to foster community growth and collective improvement.
Rapid Iteration/Pressure Cooker Development: Using tight deadlines and resource constraints to force innovative technical hacks.
The 'Smoke and Mirrors' Approach: Implementing targeted illusions that provide the perceived value of a complex system without the full overhead of a general-purpose solution.
Full-Stack Optimization: Understanding the entire system from hardware to UI to find non-obvious leverage points for performance.

dpo_pairs.prompt: What is John Carmack's view on the use of 'go to' statements in programming?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He believes they aren't poisonous and can be the right choice when language features like nested breaks are missing, although they are rare in his modern code.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He believes 'go to' statements are bad programming and should never be used in any professional codebase.
